title: Google Maps for healthcare: how practices and doctors rank higher | Rank.ai
description: How Google ranks clinics on Maps, how to set up practice, doctor and department profiles, and how to measure rank across your area.
content: In this article 9 sections Key takeaways How Google ranks clinics in the map pack Set up practice, doctor and department profiles correctly Choose categories that match how patients search Fill in the fields that help patients decide Build reviews the way Google allows Support the profile with location and service pages Measure your rank with a map scan FAQ To rank higher in Google Maps as a healthcare provider, get the profile structure right first (one profile for the practice, one for each public-facing doctor, separate profiles only for real departments), pick the most specific primary category, and build a steady flow of patient reviews. Then add a page on your website for every service and location, and measure your rank from many points around the clinic. A single search from your front desk tells you very little. Google ranks local results on three things: relevance, distance and prominence. Distance is fixed by where your patients are. Everything you can improve sits in the other two. Maps is one part of healthcare SEO , next to your website, content, reviews and AI answers. How Google ranks clinics in the map pack Google's own definitions ( Google Business Profile Help ): Factor Google's words What it means for a clinic Relevance "How well a Business Profile matches what someone is searching for" Category, services, profile description, website pages, review text Distance "How far each business is from the customer who's searching" Your verified address and pin; you can't change where patients search from Prominence "How well-known a business is," based partly on "how many reviews you have" Review count and rating, links, mentions in local news, listings on health directories Google adds that "businesses with complete and accurate info are more likely to show up in local search results." An outdated profile (old hours, a provider who left two years ago, a disconnected phone line) is an easy way to lose ground, and it also sends patients to a closed door. For the full ranking-factor picture across all industries, read how to rank higher on Google Maps and our explainer on the local pack . Set up practice, doctor and department profiles correctly Healthcare is one of the few areas where Google allows several profiles at one address. The rules in Google's guidelines for representing your business : Practice profile The organisation gets one profile for each location, under the name on its signage. Google requires a "precise, accurate address" and does not accept virtual offices or PO boxes. All locations in a country should use the same business name. Individual practitioner profiles Google names "doctors, dentists, lawyers" as examples of individual practitioners: public-facing professionals "typically with their own customer base." A practitioner can have a profile if they can be reached at the verified location during stated hours. The rules: The title should include only the practitioner's name. It "may include title or degree certification" such as Dr. or MD. A practitioner "shouldn't have multiple Business Profiles to cover all of their specializations." "Support staff should not create their own Business Profiles." A practitioner profile can rank for searches like "dermatologist near me" alongside the practice. That is useful when a doctor has a following of their own. It can also split reviews between two profiles, so decide where you will send review requests. Department profiles "Publicly-facing departments that operate as distinct entities should have their own page." Each department's name must differ from the main business and from other departments, and it should have a distinct category. Google notes such departments typically have a separate customer entrance. A hospital's emergency room, imaging centre and urgent care clinic usually qualify. A dental practice's "Invisalign service" does not. When a doctor leaves Keep the practice profile clean. Remove the departed doctor from the practice's website and provider list, update any doctor-specific profile through Google's support channels, and make sure the practice profile's photos and description no longer feature them. Choose categories that match how patients search Google asks you to use "as few categories as possible to describe your overall core business" and to make them "as specific as possible, but representative of your main business." Practice type Typical primary category Additional categories to consider General dental practice Dentist Cosmetic dentist, Dental clinic Children's dental practice Pediatric dentist Dentist Family medicine clinic Family practice physician Medical clinic Walk-in clinic Urgent care center Medical clinic Therapy group Psychologist or Mental health clinic Counselor Physical therapy clinic Physical therapy clinic Sports medicine clinic Google's category list changes over time, so check the exact names inside your profile. Pick the primary category that matches your highest-value search, then check which category the top 3 competitors for that search use. Our Google Business Profile optimization guide walks through each profile field. Fill in the fields that help patients decide A complete profile answers the questions a patient has before calling: Hours , including holiday hours and any evening or Saturday clinics. Services , written in patient language ("teeth whitening", "sports physicals"). These help relevance. Appointment or booking link , pointing to the booking page for that location. Photos of the entrance, waiting room, parking and team. Google notes that photos help you "show customers what you offer." Description of the specialties and populations you serve, without keyword stuffing. Accessibility and amenity attributes that apply, such as wheelchair access. Website link to the matching location page, so the profile and site reinforce each other. Keep the name, address and phone the same on your site, on directories (Healthgrades, Zocdoc, WebMD Care, insurer directories) and on the profile. See NAP consistency and our explainer on citation building . Build reviews the way Google allows Google says "more reviews and positive ratings can help your business's local ranking" ( Google Business Profile Help ). In a JAMA study of US adults surveyed in 2012, 37% of people who had looked up physician ratings had avoided a doctor because of bad ratings ( Hanauer et al., JAMA 2014 ). The rules: No incentives of any kind, and no asking only happy patients. Google prohibits both ( Google contribution policy ). No fake, bought or undisclosed staff reviews. The FTC's 2024 rule bans them ( FTC ). Never confirm in a reply that a reviewer is a patient. A New Jersey psychiatry practice paid $30,000 to HHS after review replies disclosed details about four patients ( HHS ). A simple system that works: send every patient the same text or email after their visit with a direct review link. The free Google review link generator creates that link. More tactics in how to get more Google reviews and healthcare reputation management . Support the profile with location and service pages Relevance comes partly from your website. Each location needs its own page with the address, map, hours, providers who work there, insurance accepted, parking notes and the services offered at that site. Each major service needs its own page too. Patients search "emergency dentist Round Rock" and "knee replacement surgeon Tampa." A page that matches the service and the place gives Google a clear reason to show the profile it is linked from. Mark both page types up with the right schema.org type: see healthcare schema markup . If you want to rank in towns where you have no office, read ranking in nearby cities . Groups with several clinics should follow multi-location SEO . Measure your rank with a map scan Search "urgent care" from the clinic's parking lot and you will likely see yourself near the top. Two miles away, a competitor closer to the searcher may take that spot. Both results are real, so a single check is misleading. A geo-grid map scan places a grid of points around your location and records your Maps rank for one keyword at each point. Rank.ai's map scan runs 3x3, 5x5 or 7x7 grids on demand, and you can try a scan free with the Google Maps rank checker . How to read the result: What the grid shows Likely cause What to do Strong at the clinic, weak a mile out Normal distance decay, weak prominence More reviews, local links, directory listings Weak even at your own address Wrong category, name issue or a duplicate profile Fix category, check for duplicates and suspensions Doctor's profile outranks the practice Reviews concentrated on the practitioner Decide which profile you want to grow and steer review requests Strong for "dentist", absent for "pediatric dentist" Category or service missing Add the service, and a category if it is a real line of care Scan again after each change and compare results over weeks. Our explainer on geo-grid rank tracking covers grid size and spacing. FAQ How do I get my medical practice on Google Maps? Create or claim a Google Business Profile for the practice at its real address, choose the most specific primary category, and complete verification. Google says verification tells it "you're authorized to represent the business." Then fill in hours, services, photos and a booking link. Should each doctor have their own Google Business Profile? Google allows it for public-facing practitioners who can be reached at the practice during stated hours. The profile name should be only the doctor's name, with an optional title such as Dr. or MD. Practices should weigh the benefit (doctor-specific searches) against splitting reviews across profiles. Why does my clinic rank well in one neighborhood and not another? Google measures distance from the searcher, so your rank changes as the searcher moves. Competitors closer to a neighborhood, or with more reviews, will often outrank you there. A geo-grid map scan shows this pattern across your whole area. Can I pay Google to rank higher on Maps? No. Google states there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. Local Services Ads and Google Ads appear in separate, labeled ad slots above or within results, and they do not change your organic map position. Do review replies affect Google Maps rankings? Google says replying "shows that you value their feedback," and that "positive reviews and helpful replies can help your business stand out." For healthcare, replies must never confirm the reviewer was a patient or discuss their care, because that can be a HIPAA disclosure. Keep replies short and invite the person to call the office.
